title: Increment a Digit List
statement:
A non-negative integer is stored as an array digits, one decimal digit per element, with the most significant digit first. There are no leading zeros, except for the number 0 itself, which is [0].

Return the digits of the number plus one, in the same format. The number can have up to 100 digits, far more than a JavaScript number can hold exactly.

examples.why: 9 + 1 = 10: write 0 and carry 1 into the 7. Adding 1 to the last digit only would give [2, 7, 10].
The carry runs off the front, so the result is one digit longer.
No carry at all: only the last digit changes and the rest are copied.

constraints: No leading zeros, except the number 0 itself
hints: Do it the way you add by hand: start from the last digit.
A digit below 9 just goes up by one and you are done. A 9 becomes 0 and the carry moves one place left.
If every digit was 9, the loop ends with all zeros and a carry still pending. Put a 1 in front.

explain.intuition:
Adding 1 only touches the run of 9s at the end. Each trailing 9 turns into 0 and passes a carry left; the first digit that is not 9 goes up by one and absorbs the carry, and everything to its left stays the same. So walk from the back, and stop as soon as a digit is below 9.

The only case that changes the length is a number made entirely of 9s: every digit becomes 0 and the carry falls off the front, so the answer is a 1 followed by zeros. Converting to a number and back is not an option: 100 digits are far beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (about 9 · 10¹⁵), so the low digits would come back wrong.
steps: Copy digits so the input is not changed.
For i from the last index down to 0: if the digit is below 9, add 1 and return the copy.
Otherwise set it to 0 and keep going left.
If the loop finishes, every digit was 9. Return [1, ...zeros].
pitfalls: Converting to a number with Number(digits.join('')). It loses precision past 15–16 digits.
Adding 1 to the last digit and stopping, which leaves a 10 in one cell.
Forgetting the all-9s case, so [9, 9] comes back as [0, 0].

solutions.title: Carry through every digit
solutions.idea: Add a carry of 1 starting from the last digit, keeping digit = sum % 10 and carry = sum / 10 for every position, like a general adder.

solutions.title: Stop at the first digit below 9
solutions.idea: Trailing 9s become 0. The first digit below 9 goes up by one and the work is done. Only an all-9s number needs a new leading 1.

followups: Add any non-negative integer k instead of 1. How does the carry loop change?
